<description>
Add a new index `txoscriptindex` which indexes all output scripts. Introduce a new `getscripthistory` RPC that returns all transactions that create outputs corresponding to the provided scripts, and optionally the transactions that spend those outputs if `txospenderindex` is also configured.

This has been a long-requested feature, attempted in previous PRs (#2802, #3652, #6835, #10370, #14053).
Some concerns raised were about the ability for an index like this to scale. I think the new techniques being used to build the indexes (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35531, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36002) alleviate this concern. This index can be synced in a few hours and the current disk usage is ~52 GB. This is less than the ~66 GB `txindex` disk usage in v31 and earlier. This index can also be used with a pruned node, so a full node can be supported in < 100 GB of disk space. Missing blocks are returned by hash and can be requested from peers using `getblockfrompeer`.

Some other previous concerns were more conceptual, that this type of index could encourage address reuse and chain analysis. IMO this ship has sailed, and the current status quo of not shipping an address index is turning off users who expect this functionality. Workarounds involve installing, configuring, and syncing other third-party software, making the UX of using Bitcoin Core in a self-sovereign way unnecessarily difficult.

The index hashes each output script with SHA256, then applies salted SipHash-1-3-UJ and stores a five-byte prefix. This is to support the popular Electrum protocol, which supplies only the script hash. The RPC can also look up by address or descriptors. Ranged descriptors are also supported, so a single RPC call can return the entire history of a receive/change xpub pair.

Because there are some scripts with millions of outputs, we introduce a new `OrderedVarInt` which serializes the block height after the script hash prefix. This lets LevelDB seek directly to the prefix + block height, so we can page by block height range.

To prevent DoS concerns by supplying an address with millions of outputs, the RPC tracks a byte budget of reads and throws immediately if too many reads are attempted. The error message instructs the user to narrow the block range.

Improvements to `txospenderindex` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36480) will also allow us to use that pruned. The end result would allow users to run with all optional indexes (including this one) in < 200 GB of disk space. Of course a larger pruned setting would be desired if many historical block lookups were being requested.
</description>

[2026-10-29] c:6499492095 comment by andrewtoth (member):
Thanks @kravens, @romanz, and @ViniciusCestarii for the reviews, and @sedited, @l0rinc, and @w0xlt for the concept ACKs!

I took some of the suggestions, and made some additional updates. This changes the index format so anyone who was testing with the previous version needs to rebuild it.

- More compact index layout for duplicate scripts in the same block. Instead of one row per output, we group all identical outputs in the same block and serialize the offsets between each of them as the value corresponding to a single key for that script and block height.
- Increase the prefix size from 5 bytes to 6 bytes. While 5 bytes is sufficient for the txindex, a collision in this index has a much worse case. If a script with none or a few outputs being looked up collides with an output that has millions of outputs, it will require scanning through all the block ranges and reading all the false positive outputs.
- Added an `asof` optional parameter to fix a blockheight when paging through requests. This let's a caller make repeated queries that set the spentness of outputs based on the `asof` block.
- Bound the undo and block reads to the lookup byte budget and throw if exceeded.
- Expose `tx_offset` from `txospenderindex` and sort spenders with it.
- Moved `TxToJSON` to `rpc/rawtransaction.h`
- Various documentation changes, including release notes.
- Added more test coverage to kill some mutants.

tACK 1fc5b618e3693c824124dd4ee4c3c95e100e645d

Re-reviewed the changes since 614302e7 (same base, no rebase). Built it and ran `txoscriptindex_tests`, `txospenderindex_tests`, `ordered_varint_tests`, `caches_tests`, `baseindex_tests`, `rpc_getscripthistory.py`, `rpc_misc.py`, `rpc_gettxspendingprevout.py`, `feature_init.py` and `feature_assumeutxo.py`. All pass.

From my earlier comments, 1 (block and undo reads outside the budget), 3 (spender ordering without a block read) and 7 (`TxToJSON` header) are fixed: `tx_to_json` now charges the serialized undo and block (`rpc/blockchain.cpp:4154`, `:4159`), `test_undo_size_limit` covers the limit, and the step-10 block read is gone. 2, 4, 5 and 6 were suggestions; no objection to leaving them.

What I checked in the new layout:

- One row per (prefix, height); the value is a run of VARINT offset deltas read until the stream is empty. `Serialize` rejects empty, non-increasing and out-of-block offsets, and `Unserialize` caps the count at `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT`. Keys, values and transaction bodies are all charged to the budget.
- `Find` keeps one block file open across rows and seeks with `SEEK_SET`, which keeps the `AutoFile` obfuscation position correct (`streams.cpp:41`). Matches still come back in (height, offset) order, so the `by_position` merge in the RPC holds.
- `CustomRemove` erases the (prefix, height) key and a competing block at the same height overwrites it; `txoscriptindex_reorg_erases_rows` covers the rewind.
- 6-byte prefix: with roughly 2^31 distinct scripts on mainnet, the chance that a queried script shares its bucket with any other script drops from about 2^-9 to 2^-17. Agree with the change.

`asof`: I read it with the paging use case in mind and could not break it. Spentness at asof comes only from the matches and txospenderindex; spenders above asof are dropped by the ancestor check at `rpc/blockchain.cpp:4097` and the output stays unspent. Reorgs above asof leave the answer unchanged, reorgs through asof fail the final check, and confirmations and times come from the asof block via `TxToUniv`, so a page stays identical while the tip moves. `test_asof` exercises all of this.

Observations, none blocking:

1. **asof could be served during the initial index sync.** `BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain()` returns false until the whole sync finishes (`index/base.cpp:444`), so a node still building either index answers nothing, even for an asof block both indexes passed long ago. The ancestor checks at `rpc/blockchain.cpp:3954` and `:3960` already guarantee that every row up to asof exists (the summary's best block lags the DB by up to 30 s during the initial sync and never leads it). Skipping the two `BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain()` calls when asof is given would let a server start paging old history while the index catches up. Fine as a follow-up.
2. **Explicit `include_mempool=true` together with `asof` is silently ignored** (`rpc/blockchain.cpp:3890`). The help text says so, but an `RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER` would make the conflict visible to a caller who set both on purpose.
3. **Release notes.** The summary mentions release notes, but the branch only touches `doc/files.md`. Did a `doc/release-notes-36629.md` miss the push?
4. **`rpc: share transaction JSON helpers` still has an empty commit body.** It changes the `getrawtransaction` help layout (`blockhash` moves below `vsize_adjusted`, `fee` moves last at verbosity 2). One line in the message would help whoever bisects a help-text diff later.
5. The "test ancestor commits" CI job died in `p2p_segwit.py` on an assertion that looks unrelated, before it reached the later commits, so the per-commit build check needs a re-run.
